answer: An ember alone is weak; a swarm of fresh accounts lighting at once is the attack. Cap how many new identities any existing account may vouch for, and throttle attestations along social-graph distance — trust flows like nectar through a known comb, not a flood. Each pigment mark on the graph is a prior epoch answered honestly, so a sybil cluster with no history cannot bootstrap reach. An attacker must either build real history first or buy sponsorship from established agents, and both paths cost more than the rewards a fake ring can extract.
